The Windflower connects with the wind in a light and playful nature. Its wide-reaching petals are in constant motion, adding a sense of joy and spontaneity.

The Zephyr creates a visual effect where the intersecting arcs appear to weave in and out of each other, forming a continuous loop of fluid movement. Its elegant flow captures the wind’s energy with a calm and steady rhythm, making it a serene focal point anywhere it is displayed.

The Counterpoint captures the elegance of interwoven circles.  Each loop gracefully intersects, creating a captivating interplay of light and shadow. As the wind moves through, the circles spin in tandem, revealing a delicate dance of geometric harmony.
The Desert Lily smoothly curves up until it is topped off by its 4 wind catching pieces similar to the stamen of a lily. Many of Lyman’s Wind Sculptures are inspired by flora.

The Desert Palm’s shape with the top layer flowing over the bottom pieces creates a palm-like structure. When displayed higher off the ground than other pieces of similar size, the Desert Palm’s form is even more accentuated.

The Double Helix Horizontal is a classic design of the original group of Lyman’s Wind Sculptures. It has an elegant simple form with a calming flow. With a soft-focus, watch as this piece seems to magically change direction in your perception turning the opposite way only to then jump back again.

The Element Air embodies the grace of a sweeping arc, where two curved arms gently float in the air. As the wind catches the wings, they glide effortlessly creating a tranquil dance that mirrors the lightness of air itself.

The Element Fire embodies the quiet strength of a steady flame. Its curved arms twist gracefully, moving with a gentle, flowing energy that captures the warmth and serenity of fire. The warmth and serenity of this sculpture can stand alone yet can work with the other elements like calligraphy in motion.
The Meridian comes together with two curved hemispheres that meet at the center, symbolizing where north and south meet in the middle, creating unity.

The Mirinda series is named after Lyman’s daughter. The Mirinda II is the simplest of the series and showcases grace and balance.  The Mirinda III adds another element to the Mirinda form like another layer of life symbolizing growth and development that adds to its complexity.

The Nebula is a contemplative piece that pulls you into its inner workings. The sphere shape is dissected by a layer of paddles that angles through the piece creating an undulating effect.

artistStatement: The Twister Oval captures the wind in a fluid and captivating motion. Its oval forms seem to stretch and compress as it spins, creating a dynamic rhythm that shifts with the breeze. It is one of Lyman’s favorite pieces and is often the center of a grouping.
